source: StreetSmart Form Review — Matt Croom's daily audit of every submitted form (full packet corpus)

latest.summary: 81 submissions reviewed for the Central calendar day of Monday 10/05/2026: 38 air job / OWL forms, 19 Trailer Inspection Forms, 8 H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Forms, 7 Trailer Readiness Forms, 4 training class forms, 2 equipment rig-down forms, 2 field service forms, and 1 ETX supervision job close-out.

concerns.title: Pablo Soto — XTO, Preston-Freeman 15I 109H / 15H 108H, trailer 608, 7:57 AM and 3:00 PM. Answered "No" to the FR uniform question on both Trailer Inspection Forms he file
concerns.text: : "They been ordered" (7:57 AM) — "Order uniforms" (3:00 PM) This reads as a supply problem rather than a refusal, but it means a technician worked a full day of wellhead air jobs out of Canon Safety issued FR. Follow-up: confirm where his uniform order stands and whether he has anything compliant to wear tomorrow.
concerns.quote: to the FR uniform question on both Trailer Inspection Forms he filed that day. He gave a reason each time, and the two reasons say the same thing:

concerns.title: 1099 Benjamin Boutte — SM Energy, Junior Mint flowback, H2S daily filed 3:09 PM. Reported a failed H2S sensor in "Comments or Concerns for Management"
concerns.text: : "Redline sencer by frac need to be swap I change batteries it still doesn't work so I just pull one from manifold till we can get a swap out." A sensor at the frac is dead after a battery change, and he has covered the gap by moving a sensor off the manifold — so the manifold position is now uncovered. He names the problem but does not name anyone notified. Follow-up: get a replacement sensor to Junior Mint and confirm who on the Permian side has been told.

concerns.title: 1099 Hayden Haugh — XTO, Friulano Huckaby 31A 1H, 4:44 PM, job 35438_2. Recorded a benzene detection after containment was broken
concerns.text: : "Crew took off the choke and installed a BPV on the wellhead. 0.05 benzene was detected after the broke containment. Crew proceeded to work after I deemed it clear." The reading is low and the control appears to have worked as intended. Logging it because it is a detection above zero. Follow-up: confirm with Haugh what the reading dropped to before the crew went back in.
concerns.quote: Crew took off the choke and installed a BPV on the wellhead. 0.05 benzene was detected after the broke containment. Crew proceeded to work after I deemed it clear.

concerns.title: 1099 Cindy Smith — XTO, Shackelford 40-12D 4H, 11:47 AM, job 35383. Recorded a second benzene detection on the same day, no numeric value given
concerns.text: : "Work area and bleeder valves tested prior to crew beginning work. No gases detected. A small amount of benzene was detected on the first break but dissipated quickly. Crew was able to work without supplied air. The job was completed according to plan without any incidents or near misses." Follow-up: ask for the actual reading. "A small amount" is not a number an auditor can work with, and the decision not to go to supplied air rests on it.

Crew was able to work without supplied air. The job was completed according to plan without any incidents or near misses.

concerns.title: Michael Jobe — XTO, Shackelford 40-12E 5H and 40-12D 4H, 11:41 AM and 11:55 AM, jobs 35382 and 35384. Reported an unauthorized person entering the exclusion zone on both
concerns.text: : "Had a guy come in our zone had to stop in tell him he couldn't be in there while work is going on" (35384) — "Crew changed out lines in had a guy come in our zone had to stop him tell him he can't be in here while work is going" (35382) Both forms selected "Unsafe conditions," which on these two is supported by the narrative. Follow-up: find out whether this was the same person twice and whether the XTO company man was told, since two incursions on one pad in one morning points at the barrier setup rather than at one individual.

concerns.title: Luis Zarate and Humberto Marquez-Salazar — XTO, Northeast Scharbauer 1219H, 3:42 PM and 3:43 PM, jobs 35388 and 35389. Zarate recorded a wellhead found in the wrong confi
concerns.text: : "Upon arrival we noticed that the master valve tree was turned in the wrong direction. Chris called the wellhead crew to come and turn it. Once it was turned we then could start reconnected wellhead." This was caught before work started and corrected, which is the system working. It is here because a master valve left the wrong way is a real pre-existing condition and should be visible to management, not because the technicians did anything wrong. Neither form selected "Unsafe conditions" for it. Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

confirm.text: Nothing on any form today recorded stop work authority being exercised. "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected on a single submission. Four forms carry selections that need the technician's confirmation before anyone treats them as events.
Selected "Unsafe conditions" together with "Stop work authority was discussed" — note that "discussed" is the routine pre-job item, not an exercise of authority:

Tyrell Sanders, XTO Friulano Huckaby 31D 4H (35437_1), 31A 1H (35438_1) and 31H 8H (35439_1). The identical ten-item selection string appears on all three of his forms, and none of the three narratives names an unsafe condition — they describe routine wellhead work and bolt condition. "Details if Any" is blank on all three. This looks like a selection carried forward from form to form rather than made fresh each time.
Selected "Unsafe conditions" with no stop-work item at all:

Ruben Rojo, XTO Pembrook Unit 906H (35428), 10:08 AM. The observe narrative is positive — "Reconnect went well with no hiccups" — but the entire OWL Learn close-out is blank and "Details if Any" is blank, so there is no written record either way. Rojo appeared on this list on 09/23/2026 under the same pattern: a selection with an empty close-out behind it.

Michael Jobe's two forms are not the mis-selection pattern and should not be read as one. He selected "Unsafe conditions" twice, and on both his narrative names a specific condition — a person walking into the live exclusion zone. That is a real item and it is written up as concern 5 above. The one question worth putting to him is whether "Stop work authority utilized" should have been selected instead of "discussed," since stopping a man and removing him from the zone is the authority being used. Jobe appeared on the 09/26/2026 list twice in one day for selecting "Unsafe conditions" with no supporting narrative; today he selected it twice with a narrative both times, which is the improvement we were asking for.
Nathan Contreras, who was on the stop-work confirmation list on 09/23 and again on 09/26, selected no stop-work or unsafe-conditions item on any of his three air jobs today.

doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Trailer 600, Humberto Marquez-Salazar, Trailer Readiness Form 4:57 PM — new finding from the late-arriving form. All ten cascade entries read "4500+". That is a pressure with no hydro date on any of the ten bottles. The combined field is meant to carry both values, and here the date half is absent across the board. Re-read directly from the source PDF to be certain. Follow-up: get the hydro dates for trailer 600's bottles recorded, since nothing in this submission establishes when any of them was last tested.

Trailer 601, Michael Jobe, Trailer Readiness Form 2:29 PM. The mirror image of the above — the four charged bottle entries carry a hydro date but no pressure: "2-23", "5-24", "1-25", "1-25". Positions 5 through 10 read "Na" and are empty bottles, which is fine. Also re-read from the source PDF; the pressure half is genuinely absent on all four.

Trailer 609, Michael Hutt, H2S daily 8:02 AM. Bottle Hydro Dates reads "N". That is not a date. Cascade pressure is complete at "1@3800/3@4400". This is the same defect Hutt filed on 09/26/2026 and it is now a repeat.

Trailer 127/148, 1099 Benjamin Boutte, H2S daily 3:09 PM. Bottle Hydro Dates reads "T/#127." — a trailer number entered in the hydro date field. Cascade pressure is complete at "2100". Boutte's recurring problem has been leaving this field blank with a trailer on location (09/26 and before); today he filled it with the wrong value. Same field, same technician, third occurrence of a problem in it.

Records that do not match the work

Billing company inconsistent between two techs on the same job, twice. On XTO Ellie 20C-29-G 4214H, Hayden Haugh billed "XTO" and Tyrell Sanders billed "Exxon". On both Shackelford jobs, Cindy Smith billed "XTO" and Michael Jobe billed "Exxon". Across the day, "Exxon" appears as the bill-to on roughly a dozen XTO Energy jobs.

Wrong well recorded inside the job body. Both forms for Friulano Huckaby 31A 1H (35438_1 Sanders, 35438_2 Haugh) carry "Friulano Huckaby 31H 8H" in the Well Location Name field, which is a different well that is also a separate job the same day (35439). Ticket 102093 is correct for 31A 1H, so this looks like a template field rather than a mis-billed job — but confirm before the tickets go out.

Jordan Lemmons ran the TXL 27 location on 10/04, so the work is real — the board just does not carry it for 10/05.

Equipment counts disagree within a single rig-down form. On Waco Kid (35442) the job header lists 10 escape packs and the closing checklist lists 6. On Waco Kid East Pad (35431) the header lists 2 monitors, 1 muster point stand and 10 escape packs while the checklist lists 1, 2 and 6. Both are Alexander Clubb's. Equipment that leaves a location uncounted is how equipment goes missing.

Joshua Blassingame's three-night Lipsey 1H supervision job closed with a total of $0.01 against pricing details of $650 per shift plus a $175 trailer charge. Timekeeping and billing anomaly rather than a safety item, but it should not reach invoicing that way.

Patrick Venson's A&R Energy NCCER/veriforce class (34904) closed on 10/05 but is a 09/21/2026 job that started 09/28 and sat paused for six days, with the pause logged from Tulsa, Oklahoma on a Seguin, Texas class. Read, but it belongs to that earlier period and is not counted toward 10/05.

Worth noting in its own right: the trailer 600 readiness form took more than twelve hours to reach the mailbox, submitted 4:57 PM and delivered 5:41 AM the next morning. Any review run the same evening will miss a form with that lag, and this one would have been reported as a missing form had the sweep not been rerun.

clean.text: Nothing requiring attention from: Justin Pack (H2S daily for Mitsui Lipsey 1H, complete hydro dates and cascade pressures, every photo taken on the day); Nathan Contreras (two Trailer Inspection Forms and the Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 603, plus three air jobs at Wilde Garner and Crouch 16 with full selections and written narratives on each); Larry Jaramillo (two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 606 and the Brunson 35 8 air job); Luis Zarate (two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 600, and the two Northeast Scharbauer and University 9 WCU jobs that caught the master valve); Andrew Bailey (three Trailer Inspection Forms and the Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 602); Hayden Haugh (two Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 607); Tyrell Sanders (Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 607); Ruben Rojo (Trailer Inspection Form for trailer 604); and Keelan Hammer (Patriot Processing

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text — so when this report says a technician photographed the fire extinguisher tag, it does not say the tag was current.

81 of 81 submissions read. The job board was available: Blake Walton's 10/5/2026 ArkLaTex & Permian Basin boards arrived at 10:11 AM Central and the 10-5 sheet of each workbook was used. 51 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 44 on the Permian board and 7 on the ArkLaTex board. The late-arrival sweep was run over the following morning through 6:30 AM Central on 10/06 and turned up exactly one submission carrying a 10/05 form date, the trailer 600 Trailer Readiness Form described above; the five other overnight arrivals are 10/06 forms and belong to today's review.
